# 0012 — Matching the ARM9 secure area (18 BIOS SWI stubs)

Status: solved 2026-11-16 (100.00 % of ARM9 code verified).

## Problem

The first 0x800 bytes of ARM9 (`0x02000000–0x02000800`, the secure area) hold
18 BIOS SWI wrapper stubs (`WaitByLoop`, `IsDebugger`, `CpuFastSet`, …,
`GetCRC16`; 4 or 6 bytes each, 76 bytes in total) between the secure-area
header and filler. They were the only unmatched functions.

Per-function translation units cannot reproduce them:

* the LCF generated by dsd puts every object section in `.text` with
  `ALIGNALL(4)`, so each TU starts on a 4-byte boundary, while 9 of the stubs
  start on halfword addresses (e.g. `CpuFastSet` at `0x02000156`);
* every CodeWarrior `asm` function is emitted in its own section, so even a
  single C file with all 18 stubs would be split and realigned;
* the bytes between the stubs are not code we write (secure-area marker and
  filler) and are not ours to commit.

## Solution

One translation unit covers the whole secure area:
`src/secure/secure_area.s`, registered in `delinks.txt` as
`.text start:0x02000000 end:0x02000800`.

* The file is assembled with **GNU as** (`arm-none-eabi-as -mcpu=arm946e-s`,
  new `gas` rule in `tools/configure.py`). One section, so only its start is
  aligned (to 4, which `0x02000000` satisfies) and every stub lands at its exact
  halfword offset.
* The stubs are written out as Thumb functions (`svc N; bx lr`, plus the two
  6-byte forms `movs r2,#0; svc 5; bx lr` and `svc 9; adds r0,r1,#0; bx lr`),
  with `.global`, `.type %function` and `.size`, so they become `FUNC` symbols
  with the same sizes as in `symbols.txt`. GNU as also emits the `$t` mapping
  symbols objdiff needs to decode them as Thumb.
* The filler between stubs is pulled at build time with
  `.incbin "extract/eur/arm9/arm9.bin", <offset>, <length>` from the user's own
  extracted binary — the same source the dsd gap objects come from — so no ROM
  bytes are committed. The `gas` build edge depends on `extract/eur/config.yaml`.

`mwasmarm` was tried first: it handles `.thumb`, `.type`/`.size` and halfword
placement, but rejects `$t`/`$d` labels, so objdiff could not tell Thumb from
ARM; GNU as produces standard mapping symbols and mwldarm links its ELF objects
like any other.

## Verification

* The assembled `.text` equals the first 0x800 bytes of `arm9.bin` exactly.
* Full build: ROM SHA-1 `52e5024e…` OK, GNU relink "all sections match",
  objdiff 7,408 / 7,408 functions, 1,422,472 / 1,422,472 bytes.
